## Body

SQLite query-selection reviews need two distinct witnesses: the selected SQL has the intended plan, and the production adapter actually selects it. PR312 R1 at 6f4c3b9010109bf5532864e48dcaa59d97603050 showed why: registry_pane_index explains exported LIST_BY_PANE_SQL directly; replacing Registry::list's pane branch with LIST_SQL still passed both committed tests. Dropping the harness predicate in the selected pane SQL did fail the behavior assertion. R312-N1 is a non-blocking C34 follow-up: drop seats_by_pane in a fresh current-schema fixture, call the actual pane-filtered Registry::list, and require its Adapter error. That cheaply connects the branch to the mandatory-index invariant.

Do not equate migration replay safety with raw SQL idempotence. CREATE INDEX without IF NOT EXISTS fails if manually repeated, while sqlx's ledger makes boot/reopen idempotent. Two successive opens of a real scratch sqlx store with 50,000 v47 rows upgraded it to v48 and preserved rows, integrity and one successful migration-48 ledger entry. The unchanged prior-version guards were replayed at SCHEMA_VERSION=47 and explicitly refused found=48 at both open and registry get. An index-only migration does not waive pij's existing directional-skew contract.

The paired constants retained SELECT *, all five numbered binds and ORDER BY id. A scratch probe extracted the real constants and compared full rows/order under 1,750 filter combinations, including empty versus absent fields and NULL columns. Folder/parent predicates were correct even though the committed pane test did not exercise them.

Harness feedback: magicWand = test the SQL that production selects, not only a public constant. Difficulty = C25 dependency-less review trees expose missing TS tooling in boot/checks; use exact-head CI plus scoped local nice-19 shared-build, without installing dependencies or symlinking node_modules. Source-archive mutants must run shared-build from the archive's own cwd, so its artifact ownership stamp describes the sources actually compiled.
